title: Beyond Transcription: Building Voice AI That Understands Conversations — Hervé Bredin, pyannoteAI
talk_summary: Hervé Bredin of pyannoteAI explains speaker diarization (who spoke when) and speaker-attributed transcription, showing that naive STT+diarization merging fails on overlaps, timestamp disagreement, and speech detected by one pipeline but not the other. Their fix is an 'exclusive diarization' step that picks the most likely speaker during overlap before reconciling with any STT model.

takeaways.technique: Reconcile outputs from two independent components with an explicit arbitration step
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of naively joining STT words to diarization turns, they run a dedicated reconciliation layer that resolves conflicts (overlaps, timestamp drift, one-sided detections) rather than trusting either source's boundaries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: STT does not transcribe overlapping speech well because the timestamps disagree between STT and diarization

takeaways.technique: Force a single winner during ambiguous overlap
takeaways.what_they_do: Their 'exclusive diarization' picks the most likely of two overlapping speakers so downstream reconciliation has one unambiguous label per region.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we find a way when there is overlap to actually select the most likely of the two speaker that will be transcribed

takeaways.technique: Benchmark on the deployment distribution, not the leaderboard distribution
takeaways.what_they_do: They show the same ASR model scoring 11.4% WER on headset-mic benchmark vs 26% on distant-mic multi-speaker data, arguing leaderboard numbers mislead for real use.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they report 11.4 % word error rate. When we apply the very same model ... we get 26%
takeaways.numbers: 11.4% WER (headset) vs 26% WER (distant mic, multi-speaker) on AMI

takeaways.technique: Decompose error into confusion / false-alarm / miss buckets
takeaways.what_they_do: Diarization error rate is reported as the sum of confusion, false alarm, and misdetection, each visualized separately so failure modes are attributable.
takeaways.numbers: 5% DER community model vs 3% precision-2 on a 30s sample

takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately avoid baking reconciliation into the STT model so it works with any STT, including customer fine-tunes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we really plan to support any kind of STT without having to change the STT model itself
